title: Data sensitivity tagging and per-stream retention controls for traces/metrics/logs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Provide a lightweight, extensible sensitivity-labeling system for observability streams (spans, metrics, logs) plus per-stream retention and access controls so teams can express data lifecycle requirements without changing instrumentation.

Scope: 
- Add a normalization layer in the ingest pipeline that attaches a "sensitivity" label (e.g., public|internal|restricted) based on rules and heuristics.
- Expose per-stream retention TTLs (e.g., 7d/30d/365d) configurable by project and by label.
- Implement RBAC for retention and label mutation (who can set/override labels/retention) and immutable audit trail for changes.
- Ensure query-time masking and storage-time redaction options for high-sensitivity streams.

Non-goals:
- Full data reingestion of historical spans for all customers (we provide targeted backfill tools, not mass reingest by default).
- Replacing application-level PII scrubbing — this complements existing scrubbing.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingest pipeline attaches sensitivity labels with >95% stability for heuristic rule set on our internal test corpus.
- Admins can set retention by project and by sensitivity label via Console and API.
- Label/retention changes are recorded in immutable audit logs with user, timestamp, and diff.
- Query-time masking works for traces/logs flagged as restricted without requiring schema changes in users' dashboards.
- End-to-end e2e tests for migration, rollback, and a canary rollout plan exist.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design rule engine and canonical label set (POC + design doc).
2) Implement ingest normalization: small stateful service that annotates events before routing to storage.
3) Storage-side TTL enforcement and tiered retention hooks.
4) Console and API surfaces for label/retention management and RBAC checks.
5) Audit pipeline that writes change events to WORM-backed audit store and exposes immutable read endpoints.
6) Gradual rollout by tenant flag, with telemetry countering (label distribution, rule false-positive/negative rates).
7) Migration/backfill toolkit for manual reclassification of stored data where required.
